Summary: The FOMC maintains a highly accommodative stance (0–0.25% policy rate, ongoing Treasury and MBS purchases, money-market operations) and emphasizes that the outlook hinges on the virus and vaccination progress. The tone is cautious and policy-supportive amid still-soft inflation and moderated activity.

Beige Book cross-check: Regional economies face pandemic-related uncertainty with near-term weakness concentrated in services; hospitality and travel are hard hit, and COVID case surges/restrictions constrain the service sector and weigh on labor markets. Offsetting pockets include stronger labor demand in manufacturing, construction, and transportation, as well as signs of solid real estate activity and vaccine-boosted business optimism for 2021.

Risk and credit lens (FSR/SLOOS): Elevated vulnerabilities (high valuations, leverage, funding fragilities) persist but are cushioned by strong bank capital/liquidity and effective facilities. Banks report tighter C&I standards and risk concerns, signaling constrained business credit supply; selective easing in mortgages and expectations for firmer consumer loan demand partially offset.

Net: The Beige Book corroborates near-term headwinds in services and employment, reinforcing a cautious stance despite vaccine-supported optimism and strength in goods-producing sectors and housing. This nudges the overall tone slightly more negative than the initial read.
